directAnswer: You can share your phone's internet connection by enabling the hotspot feature in your device's settings. This allows other devices to connect to your phone's data network.
summary: Sharing your phone's internet connection can be done through the mobile hotspot feature, which is available on most smartphones.

sections.heading: Steps for Android Devices
sections.body: The process may vary slightly depending on your Android version and device manufacturer.

sections.heading: Steps for iOS Devices
sections.body: iOS devices have a straightforward method to enable personal hotspot.

steps.title: Enable Hotspot on Android
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Network & internet > Hotspot & tethering > Wi-Fi hotspot. Toggle the switch to turn it on and configure the network name and password.

steps.title: Enable Hotspot on iOS
steps.detail: Go to Settings > Cellular > Personal Hotspot. Toggle 'Allow Others to Join' to enable the hotspot and set a password if prompted.

faqs.question: Will sharing my internet connection drain my battery?
faqs.answer: Yes, using your phone as a hotspot can significantly drain the battery, so it's advisable to keep it plugged into a charger.

faqs.question: Can I share my internet connection with multiple devices?
faqs.answer: Yes, most smartphones allow multiple devices to connect to the hotspot at the same time, but the exact number may vary by device and carrier.

faqs.question: Is there a data limit when using my phone as a hotspot?
faqs.answer: Yes, using your phone as a hotspot consumes your mobile data, and you may be subject to your carrier's data limits and throttling policies.

caveats: Data charges may apply based on your mobile plan, and excessive usage can lead to throttling by your carrier.
